Genetically programmed biotemplating enables five-orders-of-magnitude conductivity enhancement in amorphous phosphate cathodes via 3D transport networks
abstract: We demonstrate that bio-directed amorphization enables intrinsically fast ion transport in phosphate cathodes. Using genetically programmed M13 bacteriophage, we synthesize amorphous FePO 4 nanowire networks in water at low temperature, with NaCl as the only by-product. After lithiation, amorphous LiFePO 4 exhibits a 10 5 -fold conductivity increase compared to crystalline powder references, reaching σ 0 = 2 × 10 −7 S cm −1 at room temperature.

title: Hyper-Porous Membranes for Nano-Confinement-Driven Chromatographic Uranium Trapping
abstract: Most conventional membrane and ion-exchange technologies fail to efficiently remediate ultradilute radioactive actinides in complex aquatic systems because of severe charge shielding by background electrolytes and diffusion-limited kinetics. Here, we break this operational mode by demonstrating high-velocity chromatographic nano-trapping using porous amorphous covalent triazine framework (CTF) composite membranes.

title: KANA AI: A Chemical-Informed Neural Network with Hard Thermodynamic Constraints for Multicomponent Activity Coefficient Prediction
abstract: Accurate activity coefficient prediction (ln γ) for multicomponent mixtures is essential for compu-tational deep eutectic solvent (DES) discovery, yet existing methods are either thermodynamically inconsistent (black-box machine learning) or architecturally restricted to binary mixtures (hardconstraint neural networks such as HANNA). We present KANA AI, a chemical-informed neural network that embeds Gibbs–Duhem consistency, pure-component boundary conditions, permutation invariance, and Gibbs–Helmholtz consistency as hard architectural constraints, scaling to arbitrary multicomponent mixtures…

title: Experimental and Computational Studies of Intraresidue Hydrogen Bonding Mimicry of Chloroalkene Dipeptide Isosteres
abstract: Peptide bond isosteres are effective tools for investigating backbone-mediated interactions in peptides and proteins. (Z)-chloroalkene dipeptide isosteres (CADIs) have emerged as promising amide bond surrogates; however, their H-bonding properties are poorly understood. In this study we applied computational, spectroscopic, kinetic, crystallographic, electronic structure, and functional analyses to investigate the ability of CADIs to mimic intraresidue C5 H-bonds .

title: Interfacial interpenetration underlies cooperative deformation and toughness in polymer nanoparticle assemblies
abstract: Polymer materials containing numerous interfaces are often assumed to exhibit limited mechanical robustness. Here, we demonstrate that polymer nanoparticle assemblies can achieve exceptionally high toughness, with fracture strains above 1400%, tensile strengths up to 21.5 MPa, and fracture energies exceeding 80 MJ m -3 despite the presence of numerous particle-particle interfaces.

title: Interfacial structure of conjugated polymer photocatalysts with water and scavengers for sacrificial hydrogen evolution
abstract: Conjugated polymers have emerged as competitive photocatalysts for the sustainable production of hydrogen from water. Their synthetic versatility allows for systematic tuning of their opto-electronic properties and polarity to improve visible-light-driven hydrogen production. One challenge in the field is the lack of understanding of interactions of water and reactants on the molecular level with the photocatalyst. Here we probe the molecular structure of different polymer-water interfaces and link structural motifs to trends in catalytic efficiency and wettability.

title: Donor-Acceptor Conjugated Copolymers as pH-Responsive Chromatic Indicators: A TDDFT and Colorimetric Screening Study
abstract: Color change upon change of pH is a key indicator for smart packaging materials that signal food spoilage. Donor-acceptor (D–A) conjugated copolymers are attractive candidates for such indicators, as their charge-transfer transitions are highly sensitive to electronic perturbations such as protonation, an aspect that remains largely unexplored for smart packaging applications. In this study, we use DFT and TDDFT to screen 16 D–A copolymers, built from a 4×4 pairing of four donors and four acceptors, in their neutral and protonated states using the oligomer approach.

title: β-Stereoselective Glycosylation without Acyl Participation: Evaluation of β-(1→2)-Linked Disaccharide Donors and Their Application to Glycoarray Design for Antibody Characterization
abstract: β-(1→2)-Glucans constitute a relatively rare and substantially underexplored class of polysaccharides. Of particular interest is the macrocyclic β-(1→2)-glucan from Brucella (CβG), which regarded as a promising diagnostic marker of brucellosis. However, the development of CβG-based diagnostic system requires careful consideration of potential interference from short β-(1→2)-linked gluco-oligosaccharides present in various bacterial commensals and pathogens.

title: Thermo-Electrohydrodynamics of Confined Droplets
abstract: A theoretical and analytical investigation of the coupled electrohydrodynamic and thermocapillary behaviour of a confined leaky dielectric droplet suspended in an immiscible liquid medium is presented within the creeping-flow regime using the small-deformation approximation. Based on the Taylor–Melcher leaky dielectric framework, analytical solutions are obtained for the electric, thermal, and hydrodynamic fields to examine the influence of confinement, thermal Marangoni forcing, and electrical and thermal property contrasts on the interfacial stresses, flow structure, and droplet…

title: Modular Synthesis of Branched Aliphatic Aldehydes via Unified Iron-Photocatalyzed Decarboxylation and C-H Activation
abstract: We report a concise and practical method for the synthesis of branched aliphatic aldehydes via Iron-Ligand to Metal Charge Transfer (Fe-LMCT) catalysis. Fe-LMCT catalysis has emerged as a sustainable and highly versatile platform in organic synthesis by generating reactive radical intermediates from abundant chemical feedstocks. Our strategy utilizes alkyl radicals generated either via the decarboxylation of carboxylic acids or through chloride radical mediated direct hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds.

title: Detailed Microkinetics for NOx-Containing Exhaust gas conversion through Automated Mechanism Generation within Correlated Uncertainty on Pt(111)
abstract: Three-way catalytic converters simultaneously oxidize hydrocarbons and reduce NOx species. Under stoichiometric conditions the oxidation of hydrocarbons requires the transfer of oxygen from NOx species. The manner in which this occurs and the intersection of chemistry involving mixtures of C, H, N, and O atoms have not been fully explored. Experimental light-out curves reveal that stoichiometric exhaust gas containing 1000 ppm NO increases the light-out temperatures of carbon monoxide and ethene by 50 ◦C over the same exhaust mix without NOx on Pt supported on alumina.

title: Inverse theoretical spectroscopy via Monte Carlo sampling: From spectra to ensembles of molecular structures
abstract: A molecule’s structure determines its spectroscopic properties, and vice versa, molecular spectra are indispensable for elucidating its three-dimensional structure. Here, we present a Monte Carlo sampling scheme for generating an ensemble of molecular structures that is compatible with an ensemble of spectra around a given reference spectrum. By analyzing this spectrally-constrained ensemble, we can determine which structural changes are compatible with the given reference spectrum.

title: The Use of PFAS in Drug Product Presentations including Formulations, Primary and Secondary Packaging, and Delivery Devices: The Survey Conducted by the IQ Consortium Drug Product PFAS Working Group to Review the Potential Impact of PFAS Restrictions on Patient Access to Medicines
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely present across the pharmaceutical drug product supply chain, yet their role and prevalence remain incompletely characterized. An industry survey conducted by the IQ Drug Product PFAS working group (DPPFAS WG), with participation from 13 pharmaceutical companies, assessed the use and presence of PFAS across drug product modalities including oral solid dosage forms, parenteral, inhalation products, and cell and gene therapies as well as across primary and secondary packaging and drug‑delivery devices.

title: Development of a Screening Workflow for the Halogenation of Nitrogen Heterocycles with Vanadium-Dependent Haloperoxidases
abstract: The halogenation of nitrogen heterocycles is a privileged transformation for accessing important synthetic intermediates and biologically active targets in medicinal chemistry. Despite the importance of N-heterocycle halogenation, current methods rely on reagents or catalysts that are largely unselective and produce a significant amount of waste products. With an emerging interest in using halogenating enzymes to address these challenges, the vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase class of enzymes has emerged as a powerful platform for screening halogenation reactions under a uniquely large set of…

title: Ultra coarse-grained modeling of chiral molecular fluids
abstract: Molecular chirality is ubiquitous in nature and a signature of life. Understanding molecular chiral symmetry breaking has critical applications in pharmaceuticals, catalysis, functional soft materials, and biomolecular assemblies. Molecular dynamics simulations can provide insights into the microscopic mechanisms of chirality symmetry breaking, but simulations of complex molecular chiral systems at atomistic resolution remain computationally prohibitive because chirality-driven phase behavior can occur over large length and time scales.

title: Near-micron single-crystalline Mn-rich cathodes with exceptional cycling stability
abstract: Achieving high-energy-density and long-term cycling stability in Mn-redox-based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni- and Co-free Li-ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn-redox cathodes using near-micron single-crystalline δ-phase cation-disordered rocksalt (δ-DRX), derived from Mn-rich DRX, delivering an energy density of ~640 Wh kg -1 with ~97% capacity retention over 400 cycles.

title: Do electrostatic forces correlate with dispersion forces in charged molecular systems?
abstract: Electrostatic and dispersion forces in molecular systems have traditionally been considered independent, where each force arises from distinctly different mechanisms. However, ionic liquid systems, in which electrostatic interactions are particularly strong (ranging from -310 to -430 kJ mol -1 ), suggest a connection between these forces due to the significant increase in dispersion forces compared to systems comprising of neutral molecules.

title: Knowledge-Graph-Guided Design of Compositionally Flexible Alloys for Sustainable Metal Recycling
abstract: Developing engineering alloys that retain target properties despite compositional variability in mixed metallic scrap remains a major challenge in sustainable alloy design. Machine learning can accelerate alloy development, but limited datasets, extrapolation into underexplored composition spaces, and insufficient physical constraints reduce prediction reliability. To address these challenges, a recycling-oriented framework based on physicalmetallurgy knowledge graphs, termed ReAlloy-KG, is developed.

title: Molybdenum pincer complex based reduction of dinitrogen: Mechanistic bifurcation at the stage of Mo(I)-N2 intermediates
abstract: The synthesis and characterization of a new PPP ligand, bis(di-cyclopentylphosphinoethyl)phenylphosphine (PPP-Cyp), and its derived molybdenum complexes [MoBr 3 (PPP-Cyp)], [Mo≡NCl 2 (PPP-Cyp)], [Mo≡NBr 2 (PPP-Cyp)] and [Mo(η 6 -toluene)(PPP-Cyp)] are presented. The activities of these compounds towards catalytic N2RR (nitrogen reduction reaction) and reductive N2-splitting are investigated.

title: Functional Upcycling of Waste by Thermo-Electromagnetic Autocatalysis
abstract: Industrial wastes, particularly electronic wastes, pose major environmental and societal challenges owing to their rapidly increasing annual generation approaching hundreds of millions of tonnes 1 , compositional complexity, toxicity and low recycling rates 2 . Existing recovery routes are often resource-intensive and rely on large quantities of acids and bases, reaching up to 2 L kg⁻¹ of waste 3 .

title: GNN-ωPBE: Range-Separation Parameters Learned from Three-Dimensional Structures
abstract: Range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals improve density functional theory (DFT) for modeling organic semiconducting molecules by reducing self-interaction and delocalization errors, but their accuracy depends critically on the range-separation parameter (ω). Although our previously developed ML-ωPBE functional generates molecule-specific ω values from topology-based descriptors, its applicability is limited for flexible molecules with rich conformational diversity.

title: Phenomenological Prediction of Halide Perovskite Phase Stability Phenomenological Prediction of Halide Perovskite Phase Stability via Dielectric-Response Analysis: Equivalence to First-Principles Thermodynamics at Five Orders of Magnitude Reduced Computational Cost
abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid halide perovskites have achieved power conversion efficiencies exceeding 26% in single-junction solar cells, yet phase stability remains the primary bottleneck for commercialization. The cubic α-phase of FAPbI3 spontaneously transforms to the hexagonal δ-phase at room temperature, and compositional engineering through mixed cations (Cs/FA/MA) and halides (I/Br) has emerged as the dominant stabilization strategy.

title: Simultaneous Exfoliation and Nitrogen Doping of Aerosolized Graphite Oxide by Flow Through a Plasma Reactor
abstract: Continuous production of high-surface-area graphene-related materials with controllable heteroatom doping remains challenging, due to their low reactivity. Here, we demonstrate simultaneous exfoliation, reduction, and nitrogen doping of aerosolized graphite oxide (GO) in a flow-through microwave plasma reactor. Spray-dried GO powder was passed through Ar/N2 and Ar/N2/H2 plasmas operated at reduced and near-atmospheric pressures, producing reduced graphene oxide (rGO) with specific surface areas up to 700 m2 g-1.

title: Temperature-Dependent Behavior of C14-C18 Alkyl Surfactants with Ionizable and Neutral Head Groups at the Water-Decane Interface
abstract: Surfactants stabilize liquid-liquid interfaces, where adsorption is highly temperature-dependent. Interfacial shear rheology and pendant drop tensiometry were combined to study surfactant monolayers at the n-decane-water interface. Shear rheology revealed a temperature-driven phase transition, characterized by a loss of elasticity and a transition to a gas-like state. Pendant drop experiments confirmed this behavior, showing rising interfacial tension followed by plateau formation.

title: IR-DOSY: A Complementary Method to NMR-DOSY For Polymer-Size Characterization
abstract: We present a method for determining the diffusion coefficients of polymers in solution using Infrared Diffusion-Ordered Spectroscopy (IR-DOSY). We validate this approach for three distinct polymers dissolved in acetonitrile: poly(tetrahydrofuran) (polyTHF), cellulose acetate butyrate (CAB), and a styreneacrylate copolymer. The hydrodynamic radii (Rh) extracted from IR-DOSY exhibit excellent agreement with the results from complementary 1H NMR-DOSY experiments.

title: CDR-encoded recognition of Toll-like receptor 2 by a signalling-attenuating scFv
abstract: A phage-derived scFv binder, scFv33, recognizes the TLR2 LRR domain with low-tens-of-nanomolar apparent affinity and attenuates PAM3CSK4-induced cytokine transcription. Structure-informed modelling links this activity to a CDR-encoded charge–polarity–aromatic interface, providing a chemically interpretable route to TLR2-targeted immune modulation.

title: Firefly-Geni: Automated Iteration-Guided Generative Discovery of TADF Molecules
abstract: The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure-property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow.

title: Unified chemical memory and computation in a single-molecule nanoreactor
abstract: Molecular systems can store data, and chemical reaction networks can form reservoirs for computation, but architectures that integrate both functions remain elusive. Here we show that a single nanopore can both store and process information by using its own chemical dynamics. Confined in an individual protein nanopore acting as a nanoreactor, reactive cysteine residues on a single β strand encode ‘1’ bits, and unreactive residues encode ‘0’ bits – together constituting configurable memory tapes.

title: Influence of Ligand Rigidity and Steric Bulk on Reductions of Tridentate NON-Diamido Alkaline Earth Metal Complexes
abstract: Structural modifications to tridentate NON ligands have been shown to play a key role in controlling the outcomes of group 2 metal diamide reduction reactions. Herein, two bulky, geometrically flexible diamines, F NON Ar H 2 ( F NON Ar H 2 = O{2-N(H)Ar-4- t BuC 6 H 3 } 2 ; Ar = 2,4,6- i Pr 3 C 6 H 2 (Trip); 2,4,6-Cy 3 C 6 H 2 (TCHP)), have been synthesised. Treatment of F NON Trip H 2 with one equivalent of either BePh 2 , Mg{CH 2 (SiMe 3 )} 2 , or Ca{N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } 2 in methylcyclohexane yielded group 2 metal diamide complexes.

title: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for GPU Materials Science
abstract: Despite significant progress in large language models (LLMs) with general reasoning capabilities, their adaptability remains limited in interdisciplinary domains that require specialized expertise, such as materials science. To address this gap, this study constructs a domain-specific benchmark for GPU materials science, comprising a systematically curated evaluation dataset and a comprehensive assessment of representative LLMs on domain-specific tasks.

title: Exploiting Ruthenium(II) Polypyridyl Complexes to Advance Intracellular Photoredox Catalysis as an Antimicrobial Strategy
abstract: As antibiotic resistant infections become ever more prevalent, the WHO has designated the antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis as a silent epidemic. With over 1.1 million deaths directly caused by AMR in 2021 and a further 4.7 million associated deaths annually, there has never been a more pertinent time to investigate novel drug modalities and methods to tackle these challenging infections.

title: Scanning lanthanoid magnetic susceptibility tensors by spy molecules using paramagnetic fast magicangle spinning NMR spectroscopy
abstract: Magnetic properties of lanthanoid ions at the atomic level are challenging to derive despite the wealth of chemical and structural information encoded in them. We herein report protondetected paramagnetic solid-state NMR experiments at magic-angle spinning frequencies of 100 kHz and more that allow to scan the magnetic susceptibility tensors of europium(III)-based π-containers in the solid state, which have initially been determined in solution.

title: Designing Ultrasmall Nb-doped Alloy and Nanocomposite Ir Electrocatalysts for Oxygen Evolution
abstract: Developing durable, low-Ir-content catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to advancing green hydrogen production. Here, we explored Nb incorporation as a strategy to reduce Ir usage and investigated its impact on OER performance. By exploiting the redox properties of different solvents in a simple solvothermal synthesis, we prepared two distinct Nb-Ir catalyst systems. 5 nm alloy nanorods with Ir and Nb mixed on the atomic scale were prepared using highly reducing solvents, while <2 nm decahedral Ir/NbOx composites formed in less reducing media.

title: A Descriptor for Non-Arrhenius Ion Transport Enables Design of Sulfide Superionic Conductors
abstract: Solid electrolytes are central to the realization of safe, high-energy all-solid-state batteries, yet their practical deployment is still constrained by an incomplete understanding of ion transport across broad temperature ranges. In sulfide solid electrolytes, deviations from classical Arrhenius behavior are increasingly observed, but such non-Arrhenius transport is rarely quantified in a way that can be generalized, interpreted chemically, or incorporated into materials design.

title: Quantitative Pathway-Resolved Kinetics from Neural Network-Guided Weighted Ensemble Simulations
abstract: Many crucial biomolecular processes, such as ligand dissociation and conformational switching, occur via multiple competing transition pathways. While standard rare-event sampling methodologies provide rigorous estimates of the global transition rate, they typically collapse the underlying mechanistic heterogeneity into a single global constant, obscuring the relative kinetic contributions of distinct channels.

title: Reaction Dynamics of OH + SiH4 → H2O + SiH3: A Quasi-Classical Trajectory Study on the PES-2022 Surface
abstract: A quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) study is presented of the OH + SiH 4 → H 2 O + SiH 3 hydrogen-abstraction reaction on the full-dimensional analytical potential energy surface PES-2022. A total of 1.8 million trajectories were run at seven fixed collision energies (Ecoll = 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 kcal mol−1), yielding more than 28 000 DZPE reactive trajectories. The integral reactive cross section σ(E) rises from 0.56 Å 2 at E = 0.5 kcal mol −1 to a plateau near 4.9 Å 2 above E = 6 kcal mol −1 .

title: Time-resolved Green Chemistry Metrics for Low Energy Depolymerization of Polyethylene Terephthalate
abstract: For the circular utilization of plastics such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), chemical recycling has emerged as a promising approach for processing diverse waste streams. Methanolysis is particularly advantageous because impurities in the monomer dimethyl terephthalate can be readily removed by purification. Recently, methanolysis aided by equilibrium-shifting reagents has attracted attention as an efficient depolymerization strategy. Comprehensive evaluation of such systems remains challenging, however, because reaction efficiency depends on multiple factors.

title: DATA-DRIVEN CAUSAL DISCOVERY IN CATALYSIS
abstract: Catalysts are essential for the transition towards more sustainable chemical processes. However, their design still relies largely on empirical strategies, limiting the systematic understanding of how synthesis variables and reaction conditions influence catalytic performance and final material properties. This work applies causal discovery methods to two catalytic case studies: an OCM reaction dataset and an in-house dataset on metal-supported zeolite synthesis.

title: Regioselective distal C(4)–H arylation of naphthalene directed by simple acetamido group at position C(2)
abstract: Herein, we report preferential C(4)-arylation of the naphthalene in N-(naphthalen-2-yl)amides is with aryl halides in the presence of a palladium catalyst and silver salt under mild reaction conditions. The developed efficient protocol yields C(4)-arylated naphthylamides in good to high yields with broad functional group tolerance. Silver salt, in particular silver carbonate, was found to be crucial for catalytic cycle, regenerating palladium catalyst most probably as iodide scavenger.

title: PolyDiT: Masked Diffusion Transformers for Polymer Generation and Property Prediction
abstract: Polymer repeat unit representation is not neutral preprocessing for diffusion models because it defines the feasible set, constraint locality, and chemical granularity of denoising. We introduce PolyDiT, a bidirectional discrete Diffusion Transformer (DiT) framework that learns polymer generation and propertypredictive features through masked reconstruction of representation-indexed polymer states. PolyDiT compares SMILES, SMILES byte pair encoding (SMILES-BPE), SELFIES, Group SELFIES, and graph states while holding the masking schedule, sampling protocol, and property head protocol fixed.

title: Physics-guided modelling of temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of functional oxides
abstract: Functional oxide materials are widely employed across a range of electronic applications, where electrical conductivity and its temperature dependence serve as key screening metrics for material suitability. Across these applications, experimental characterisation remains resource-intensive and time-consuming. As a result, machine learning approaches have recently emerged as a digital alternative to accelerate materials discovery processes.

title: Engineered Fluids Unlock Coupled Geological Hydrogen and Critical Mineral Recovery from Ultramafic Rocks
Development of a High Throughput Automated Titration System Relevant for Extraction of Critical Metals
abstract: An accurate determination of the acidity (pKa) of extractants in biphasic solvent systems is crucial, as this physicochemical property impacts efficiency and selectivity in the recovery of technologically critical metals. The conventional manual or semi-automated titrations used for this purpose frequently require substantial human input to operate continuously.

title: Ratiometric Luminescent Thermo-Hygrometry, Metal-Dependent Second Harmonic Generation, and Humidity-Variable Magnetic Relaxation in a Manganese(II)-Doped Zinc(II) Molecular Halide
abstract: Molecular materials based on metal complexes can link optical, electrical, and magnetic properties, all sensitive to external stimuli. This feature opens a pathway for their exploration as highly efficient sensors and advanced switches. We report the synthetic strategy for a truly multifunctional material linking dual-stimuli optical sensing with tunable non-linear optical activity and chemically modulated magnetic response.

title: Direct Determination of the Acidity of Organophosphorus Extractants in Nonpolar Organic Solvents Using Biphasic Potentiometric Titrations
abstract: The current revolution in artificial intelligence (AI) has catalyzed global demand for electronic components and the critical metals that make up these electronic systems. This new demand has increased strain on the already thinly stretched global supply chains that provide the materials for electronic components. Innovation in the field of critical metal separation can help to relieve supply train stress and provide the required critical materials more efficiently.

title: Memory-Aware SIMD-Enabled Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Code-Generation Procedure: Acceleration of the MB-pol Potential Energy Function as an Example
abstract: Permutationally invariant polynomials have been used to develop a variety of highly accurate potential energy surfaces. Particularly when combined with the many-body expansion, such potentials present a promising avenue for reducing the computational cost of simulations with coupled-cluster accuracy. In practice, performing molecular dynamics simulations with many-body polynomial potential energy functions requires evaluating the polynomial and its gradients thousands of times at each simulation step.

title: Direct Photocatalytic Synthesis of 1,3,4-Oxa(thia)diazoles from aldehydes and (thio)hydrazides.
abstract: 1,3,4-Oxa(thia)diazoles have a great interest in different areas of chemistry. Despite the different methodologies reported in the literature, a general approach under mild photocatalytic conditions would broaden the applications of these molecules. Here we report a visible-light photocatalytic synthesis of 1,3,4-oxadiazoles and 1,3,4thiadiazoles from readily available aldehydes and (thio)hydrazides using an acridine photocatalyst under mild conditions. The scope was found to be broad, and gram-scale synthesis was achieved.

title: FIREX: Fast-Ion Replica EXchange enables rapid sampling of Mg2+ pairing with nucleic acids
abstract: We introduce Fast-Ion Replica EXchange (FIREX), a Hamiltonian Replica Exchange-based sampling strategy specifically designed to enhance the sampling of metastable divalent cation binding with phosphate groups, e.g., in nucleic acids. We parametrize the scheme and demonstrate its convergence and efficiency on a model DNA dodecamer with Mg2+ ions, using two force fields with very different ion-pairing properties to test its robustness.

title: Modelling Mixture Permeation across Microporous Membranes using the Maxwell-Stefan Diffusion Formulation
abstract: Binary mixture diffusion in microporous crystalline materials is characterized by a set of three M-S diffusivities: Ð1, Ð2, and Ð12. The Maxwell-Stefan (M-S) diffusivities Ð1, and Ð2 characterize interactions of guest molecules with pore walls. The exchange coefficient Ð12 quantifies correlation effects that result in slowing-down of the more mobile species due to correlated molecular jumps with tardier partners.

title: Recent Advances in Sodium-Ion Diffusivity in Sodium-Ion Batteries: Mechanisms, Characterization Techniques, Materials Design, and Future Perspectives
abstract: One of the fundamental kinetic parameters governing the electrochemical performance of sodium-ion batteries is Ion Diffusivity. Though sodium-ion batteries have advantages when it comes to cost, sustainability, and material abundance in comparison to lithium-ion batteries, their widespread application is hindered by sluggish Na+ diffusion that is caused by the larger ionic radius and higher migration barriers of sodium ions.

title: Stability Trends of Surface and Subsurface Interstitial Transition Metal Species on CeO2(111)
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) on reducible oxides are generally assumed to consist of isolated metal atoms located at the surface and directly accessible to reactants. Recent studies on Pt/CeO 2 (111), however, revealed that Pt preferentially occupies subsurface interstitial sites. Here, we investigate whether this behavior is unique to Pt or represents a more general phenomenon. Using density functional theory, we systematically compare the stability of surface and subsurface configurations for transition-metal atoms from Fe to Au on stoichiometric CeO 2 (111).

title: PARSEC.py: A Python-based Real-space Kohn–Sham Density Functional Theory Code Accelerated by Machine Learned Charge Density
abstract: PARSEC.py is a Python-based real-space Kohn–Sham density functional theory (real-space KS-DFT) framework designed to provide a user-and developer-friendly platform for firstprinciples electronic-structure simulations. Discretization on real-space grids eliminates basisset approximations, while enabling systematic control of numerical accuracy and large-scale parallelization. Building upon the theoretical foundations of the original PARSEC code, the framework leverages the Python scientific ecosystem to support modular development and integration with modern machine learning (ML) tools.

title: Total Syntheses of Tricrilactones D and F, Crispatumine I and 2,3-trans-Crispatumine I; a Bio-inspired Three-Component Cascade to Access the Lactone-fused 9/5/6 Spirocyclic Framework
abstract: Tricrilactones B-F and crispatumines G-K, anti-osteoporotic macrolides isolated from Trichocladium crispatum , all possess a unique 9/5/6 spiroketal-containing tricycle fused to a substituted lactone. We herein report the total syntheses of tricrilactones D and F, crispatumine I, and an anticipated natural product, 2,3- trans -crispatumine I. Our approach constructs the conserved 9/5/6 spirocyclic core in a single step via a three-component biomimetic cascade of protrilactione A, the purported biosynthetic precursor, reacting with an aldehyde and ß-ketolactone.

title: Deep Learning-driven synergistic engineering of PET hydrolase for post-consumer PET depolymerization
abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) offers a promising route to mitigate the increasingly severe problem of plastic pollution. However, the development of highly efficient PET hydrolases capable of processing post-consumer PET remains a critical challenge. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) provide new opportunities to accelerate the enzyme engineering of PET hydrolases. Here, we report a systematic computational redesign of the PET hydrolase NI (ThcCut1-AICCG-H185N/F189I) using the deep-learning framework, EITLEM-Kinetics. By integrating mutation free-energy constraints with kinetic parameter prediction, the framework enables simultaneous optimization of catalytic activity and thermostability. A total of nine beneficial substitution sites were identified and experimentally validated that overcoming the activity-stability trade-off. Combinatorial iteration yielded an optimal variant, NI-E65K/H107Y/A2R/L33F (NI-KYRF), which exhibited an 80% and 90% increase in depolymerization activity toward Gf-PET film and one-step pretreated post-consumer PET (pc-PET powder), respectively, along with a 2.61 °C increase in melting temperature (T m). NI-KYRF displayed a specific activity of 665 μmolTPAeq h-1 mgenzyme -1, representing 2.0- and 1.48-fold improvements over representative high-performance PET hydrolases ICCG and TurboPETase. The depolymerization performance of NI-KYRF towards various post-consumer PET wastes and polyester plastics was significantly improved. At 70 °C, it achieved a 95.5% depolymerization conversion of pc-PET powder within 24 h, and for untreated post-consumer PET film, the conversion reached 80.1%, representing a 2.1-fold improvement in depolymerization efficiency over the parental NI. In addition, enhanced activity toward polyesters plastics, including PBAT and PBT, indicates an expanded substrate scope. Molecular dynamics simulations and structural analysis reveal that these mutations enhance enzyme performance through synergistic mechanisms. Overall, this study establishes a deep learning-guided computational design framework based on EITLEM-Kinetics and demonstrates its effectiveness and broad potential for engineering high-performance PET hydrolases.

title: Twist-configured moire-moire reconstruction governs diverse commensurate double-moire phases in twisted bilayer graphene on h-BN
abstract: The coexistence of multiple moire lattices in van der Waals heterostructures raises a fundamental question: how do distinct moire patterns interact and reconstruct? Here, we investigate twisted bilayer graphene (tBG) on hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), where tBG and graphene/h-BN moire structures coexist, using conductive atomic force microscopy combined with continuum-model simulations. We show that reconstruction between these moire lattices-moire-moire reconstruction-manifests across multiple length scales, giving rise to diverse commensurate double-moire phases. Locally, the stacking registry between the two moire lattices is uniquely selected by the global twist configuration (helical or alternate), mediated by rotational relaxation of the shared graphene layer. This registry, together with twist angle and strain, governs commensurate domains from C3z-symmetric to strained symmetry-modified structures. These results establish moire-moire reconstruction as a general framework for engineering structural and electronic order -- including theoretically predicted topological flat bands below the magic angle -- in multilayer moire materials.
